 Dale Earnhardt Jr. Teases Carson Hocevar Racing for JR Motorsports in 2027
 November 9, 2026 
 3:14 pm 
 News 
 Josh Mull 
 Photo by Meg Oliphant/Getty Images 
 About the Author
 Josh Mull 
 View Stories 
 Join the Conversation
 Instagram 
 Facebook 
 Youtube 
 Tiktok 
 Discord 
 What’s Happening?
 Dale Earnhardt Jr. wants Carson Hocevar behind the wheel of a JR Motorsports car in the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series next season. During an appearance Monday, Dale told fans that he plans to get the Spire Motorsports driver into one of his cars in 2027.
 Dirty Mo Media shared Dale’s comment Monday, with the crowd erupting at the possibility of Hocevar racing for JRM.
 JRM has already revealed plans to bring Spire drivers into its O’Reilly Series program next season.
 No official agreement, car number, or race schedule has been announced for Hocevar.
 “We’re gonna get Hocevar to race one of our (JRM) cars next year,” Dale said.
 “We’re gonna get Hocevar to race one of our (JRM) cars next year” -Dale
Whole crowd went wild 😂 pic.twitter.com/riCQW3ucSV 
— Dirty Mo Media (@DirtyMoMedia) November 9, 2026 
 JRM Already Has Plans With Spire
 The idea isn’t coming out of nowhere. Last week, JRM co-owner Kelley Earnhardt Miller revealed that the team expects to have drivers from Spire Motorsports in its cars next season .
 JRM is already working with Spire development driver Tristan McKee, who signed a multi-year agreement with the team in October . McKee will make his O’Reilly Series debut in the No. 9 Chevrolet at Bristol next August, with plans to gradually increase his schedule before going full-time in 2029.
 That leaves opportunities for other drivers to share the No. 9, and JRM has already discussed bringing in drivers from both Spire and Trackhouse Racing. Hocevar would be an interesting addition to that rotation.

 Could Hocevar Race for JRM in 2027?
 The timing is particularly interesting for Hocevar, whose 2026 Cup Series season ended with a suspension from Spire Motorsports following his controversial brake-checking of Austin Cindric at Martinsville.
 Despite that rough ending, Hocevar remains one of Spire’s most important drivers. He won his first Cup Series race at Talladega this season, and the team signed him to a long-term contract earlier this year that extends into the next decade.
 Dale’s comments suggest there could be an opportunity for Hocevar to add some O’Reilly Series starts to his schedule while continuing to race full-time for Spire in Cup. But there’s still a difference between Dale telling fans he wants to make it happen and JRM announcing an actual deal.
 For now, we know Dale wants Hocevar in one of his cars next year, and JRM already has plans to work with Spire drivers. We’ll have to see whether that turns into an official announcement.
